cards.text: Soon afterward, Jesus heads to a town called Nain, and He's got company. When I go somewhere, it's me, my gold base and my mustache, and the mustache is doing ALL the heavy lifting.

cards.question: Who's walking with Jesus on the way to the town of Nain?

answers.text: His disciples and a large crowd

cards.text: As Jesus gets close to the town gate, something is coming out the other way. It's a dead man, being carried out of town.

cards.question: The dead man being carried out of Nain is the ___ son of his mother.
The dead man's mother still has her husband to lean on.

cards.text: She's a widow, and he was her only son. A large crowd from the town is walking with her, and I bet every one of them is hurting for her.

cards.question: When the Lord sees the grieving widow at the gate, what does He have for her?
Then Jesus speaks to the widow. What does He tell her?

cards.text: Then Jesus goes right up to the funeral procession and touches the coffin. In front of BOTH crowds.

cards.question: What do the men carrying the coffin do when Jesus touches it?
With His hand on the coffin, Jesus speaks again. Who is He talking to this time?

answers.text: The young man in the coffin

cards.text: "Young man," He said, "I tell you, get up!" That's the whole thing. Friend, I give a LONGER pep talk to my oven before I preheat it.

cards.question: After Jesus speaks, the dead man sits up and begins to speak.
Then Jesus gives the young man back to his ___.
A sense of awe sweeps over everyone there, and they glorify God.
The people say a great ___ has appeared among them.

cards.text: And they say, "God has visited His people!" Meanwhile it takes me THREE alarms and a pep talk to get moving in the morning. That young man got up on ONE sentence.

cards.question: The news about what Jesus did stays inside the town of Nain.

findings.problem: The joke's comparison doesn't match the fact. In the passage, Jesus is traveling with a crowd of people. In the joke, Papa Dorin travels with his own base and mustache, which aren't company, and 'the mustache is doing ALL the heavy lifting' has nothing to do with being accompanied. A stranger would say 'huh?' The joke also leans on the mustache, which is supposed to be a fact about him rather than his source of jokes.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The mustache is used as the punchline of the joke.

rule.text: The mustache is a fact about him, not his main source of jokes.

findings.problem: Card 6 opens by restating that she's a widow and he was her only son. Cards 4 and 5 just asked about both facts, so half the card is a recap rather than the next moment of the passage.

The wrong answer 'The widow beside the coffin' is true elsewhere in the passage. Jesus does speak to the widow in Luke 7:13. Only the words 'this time' make it false, so it's false at this moment but not anywhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: 'With His hand on the coffin' says His hand stays on the coffin while He speaks. Luke 7:14 only says He touched the coffin.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card cites Luke 7:16, but its joke is about the young man getting up after one sentence, which uses Luke 7:14-15. The card's citation doesn't cover every verse it uses. The joke also pulls the baker back to an earlier moment instead of riding along with the praise in verse 16.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The passage's last detail, that the news spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region (Luke 7:17), is never told. The baker only learns that the news didn't stay in Nain, so they leave without knowing how far it went.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question types follow a visible pattern. Cards 7, 8, 10 and 11 are a run of multiple choice, then cards 13 to 16 alternate true or false and fill in the blank (TF, FB, TF, FB) before ending on another true or false.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: Card 17 repeats card 12's joke. Both say Papa Dorin needs a long pep talk to get something going, while Jesus needed one short sentence. The second one reads as the same punchline again rather than a callback that builds on the first.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin be allowed to reuse the same joke premise twice in one lesson, or should a repeat only count as a callback when it adds a new twist?
